title: Steering Diffusion Models Towards Credible Content Recommendation
claim: Conditional diffusion for sequence modeling uses encoded context as the condition and the target embedding as the diffusion target.
layout: Single panel, top-down then right-to-left; dashed reverse path, solid forward path
description: A single diagram of a general diffusion-based sequential recommendation paradigm. A blue arrow across the top is labeled "A user's interaction sequence". Below it, yellow circles for context item embeddings e1, e2, ..., e_{n-1} sit inside a dashed rounded box. Arrows run from them down into a light-blue "Sequence Encoder" box. A pink circle for the target item's embedding e_n sits at the right. A dashed arrow runs from e_n down to e_n^0 in the bottom-right corner. The bottom row is a chain of circles going right to left, e_n^0, e_n^{t-1}, e_n^t, ..., e_n^T, with the colors darkening to brown. Solid "Forward" arrows point left. A dashed "Reverse" arrow points right. The encoder output arrow is labeled "Condition" and curves into the reverse step.
caption: A general paradigm of DM-based sequential recommendation methods. The condition and diffusion target (i.e., target item’s embedding) are two core components in DM-based methods.
abstract: In recent years, diffusion models (DMs) have achieved remarkable success in recommender systems (RSs), owing to their strong capacity to model the complex distributions of item content and user behaviors. Despite their effectiveness, existing methods pose the danger of generating uncredible content recommendations (e.g., fake news, misinformation) that may significantly harm social well-being, as they primarily emphasize recommendation accuracy while neglecting the credibility of the recommended content. To address this issue, in this paper, we propose Disco, a novel method to steer diffusion models towards credible content recommendation. Specifically, we design a novel disentangled diffusion model to mitigate the harmful influence of uncredible content on the generation process while preserving high recommendation accuracy. This is achieved by reformulating the diffusion objective to encourage generation conditioned on preference-related signals while discouraging generation conditioned on uncredible content-related signals. In addition, to further improve the recommendation credibility, we design a progressively enhanced credible subspace projection that suppresses uncredible content by projecting diffusion targets into the null space of uncredible content. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of Disco in terms of both accurate and credible content recommendations.
